task_1.title: Support untagged CPython builds with trailing plus versions
task_1.description: Poetry 1.8.3 adds compatibility for untagged CPython interpreters that report a full version ending in '+'. The upgrade normalizes the full Python version used for environment markers so dependency and environment checks treat these builds as the corresponding standard CPython release.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that untagged CPython builds whose reported full version ends with a trailing '+' are accepted and interpreted as the corresponding standard Python release when Poetry evaluates environment and dependency markers.

expectation.grounded: If `platform.python_version()` returns a version string with a trailing `+`, Poetry should expose `python_full_version` without that suffix in marker environments produced by `SystemEnv.get_marker_env()` and in the generated environment script data. `python_version` should continue to reflect the existing major.minor value.
expectation.conceptual: Poetry should treat untagged CPython interpreters that append '+' to their version string as the same release without the suffix when determining Python-version-based compatibility.

constraints.grounded: Only the terminal `+` on the full interpreter version should be normalized. Existing behavior for already-normal version strings and unrelated marker fields must remain unchanged, and the normalized `python_full_version` should be consistent across both direct and script-derived marker environments.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to smoothing over the special CPython version suffix and should not change how standard Python versions or unrelated environment metadata are interpreted.

behavior: When Poetry reads an interpreter version such as `3.11.9+`, the exposed `python_full_version` becomes `3.11.9` rather than preserving the trailing `+`.
The same full-version normalization applies whether marker data is produced directly from the active system environment or from generated script-based environment inspection.
Major.minor `python_version` handling remains the same; the change affects only the full-version representation used for marker evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry runs on a CPython build whose reported full version ends with `+`, it should present `python_full_version` without the trailing `+` in its marker environment.
When dependency or environment markers rely on `python_full_version` for such an interpreter, they should observe the normalized release version rather than a `+`-suffixed variant.
When Poetry runs on interpreters whose reported version does not end with `+`, it should preserve the existing marker behavior unchanged.
When marker environment data is obtained through either the in-process environment model or generated script-based inspection, both paths should report the same normalized `python_full_version`.

task_3.title: Handle FIPS-restricted MD5 dependency hashes
task_3.description: Poetry 1.8.3 fixes dependency artifact hash calculation on FIPS-enabled systems. If a dependency link only exposes an MD5 hash and the runtime disallows MD5 initialization, the repository should skip that unusable known hash and continue calculating SHA256 instead of failing early.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency downloads remain processable on FIPS-enabled systems when a package link advertises an MD5 hash that the runtime refuses to initialize, instead of failing before SHA256 can be calculated.

expectation.grounded: When `HTTPRepository` evaluates a dependency link hash, failure to instantiate the selected known hash algorithm because it is unavailable or disabled, including MD5 under FIPS restrictions, should not abort hash calculation. The repository should continue with SHA256 calculation and return the SHA256 result for the artifact.
expectation.conceptual: If the environment blocks a legacy hash algorithm advertised by a package source, dependency resolution and artifact verification should fall back to a supported SHA256 calculation rather than erroring out solely because that legacy hash cannot be created.

constraints.grounded: Supported hash algorithms must continue to be used when available. Links with no usable known hash must still produce the same SHA256 output path. Only failures caused by unavailable or disabled hash constructors should be bypassed; normal download and SHA256 calculation behavior must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to hash-algorithm availability problems and must not change successful hashing flows or the resulting SHA256-based artifact identification.

behavior: If the highest-priority link hash algorithm cannot be instantiated because the runtime disables it or the algorithm is unavailable, hash initialization is skipped instead of raising an immediate failure.
A dependency link that provides only an MD5 hash remains processable on FIPS-enabled systems by continuing to compute SHA256 for the downloaded artifact.
Dependency links that already provide a supported hash, such as SHA256, continue through the existing hashing flow without behavioral change.
Links without usable known hashes still yield a SHA256-based artifact hash rather than failing during known-hash setup.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency link advertises only an MD5 hash and the runtime rejects MD5 because FIPS mode is enabled, calculating the artifact hash should succeed and produce a SHA256-based result.
When the selected known hash algorithm is unavailable in the runtime, dependency hash calculation should continue without raising an error from hash-constructor initialization alone.
When a dependency link advertises a supported hash algorithm, artifact hash calculation should behave as before and still complete successfully.
When no usable link hash can be initialized, the system should still calculate SHA256 for the downloaded artifact.

task_4.title: Raise an error for unsupported wheel metadata versions
task_4.description: Poetry 1.8.3 stops silently treating wheels with unsupported package metadata versions as packages with no dependencies. Instead, wheel inspection now fails explicitly with a package info error so dependency resolution does not proceed with incomplete metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that wheels with unsupported or unrecognized package metadata versions are rejected explicitly instead of being interpreted as having empty dependency metadata.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry inspects a wheel via PackageInfo.from_wheel, it should validate the distribution metadata_version before building PackageInfo data. If the metadata version is not supported by pkginfo, the operation must raise PackageInfoError rather than returning an empty PackageInfo or silently exposing no dependencies. For supported metadata versions, dependency extraction from wheel metadata should continue to behave as before.
expectation.conceptual: When Poetry reads dependency information from a wheel, unsupported metadata formats should produce a clear failure instead of making the package look dependency-free. Supported wheel metadata should continue to resolve package information normally.

constraints.grounded: Do not silently fall back to empty package metadata or an empty dependency list when wheel inspection fails because the metadata version is unknown. Limit the new failure behavior to unsupported metadata-version cases and preserve existing successful behavior for wheels with recognized metadata versions.
constraints.conceptual: Do not hide metadata parsing failures by substituting incomplete package information. Only packages using unsupported metadata formats should fail; valid wheels should remain unaffected.

behavior: Wheel package inspection now checks whether the parsed metadata_version is recognized before reading dependency metadata.
If a wheel uses an unsupported or unknown metadata version, Poetry raises PackageInfoError instead of returning a blank package info object.
Unsupported wheel metadata no longer appears to dependency resolution as an empty dependency set.
Wheels with supported metadata versions continue to expose their package information and dependencies through normal inspection.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry inspects a wheel whose metadata version is supported, it should return package information and dependencies normally.
When Poetry inspects a wheel whose metadata version is unsupported or unknown, it should raise PackageInfoError instead of treating the wheel as having no dependencies.
When dependency resolution encounters a wheel with unsupported metadata, the failure should be surfaced explicitly rather than silently omitting that package's dependencies.

task_5.title: Handle Trailing Slashes In Git Source URLs
task_5.description: Poetry 1.8.3 fixes git URL handling so repository names are derived correctly when a git dependency source URL ends with a trailing slash. This prevents valid git sources from being interpreted inconsistently solely because of URL formatting.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that git dependency source URLs ending with a trailing slash are handled the same as equivalent URLs without the trailing slash when deriving the repository name.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry derives a repository name from a git source URL through `Git.get_name_from_source_url()`, it should ignore any trailing `/` before extracting the final path segment and continue removing an optional `.git` suffix from that segment. Git URLs that differ only by a trailing slash should therefore resolve to the same repository name.
expectation.conceptual: Git-based dependency sources should behave consistently whether or not the configured URL ends with a trailing slash. A valid repository URL must still resolve to the same package or repository name regardless of that formatting difference.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve existing name derivation for git URLs that already work without a trailing slash, including forms that already end with `.git`. Only terminal slash normalization should affect the derived name; other URL content and naming rules should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: This fix should be limited to normalizing trailing slashes and must not alter how other valid git URLs are interpreted.

behavior: Repository name extraction for git source URLs now trims a trailing slash before selecting the last path segment.
The optional `.git` suffix is still removed from the extracted repository segment after trailing-slash normalization.
Equivalent git URLs with and without a trailing slash now produce the same derived repository name.
acceptance_criteria: When a git dependency source URL ends with a trailing slash, it should derive the same repository name as the equivalent URL without the trailing slash.
When a git dependency source URL ends with `.git`, the derived repository name should omit that suffix whether or not the URL also has a trailing slash.
When a git dependency source URL does not end with a trailing slash, its repository name derivation should remain unchanged from prior behavior.

task_2.title: Support package metadata version 2.3
task_2.description: Poetry 1.8.3 raises its minimum pkginfo dependency so it can understand package metadata version 2.3 and avoid failing package inspection on newer distributions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency handling can process packages whose distribution metadata uses version 2.3, instead of failing during package inspection or package creation when those packages are encountered.

expectation.grounded: Poetry 1.8.3 must require pkginfo 1.10 or newer so that packages declaring metadata version 2.3 are supported during package information extraction. When such a package is inspected for dependency resolution or installation, Poetry should obtain the metadata needed to create the package representation rather than failing because the package information could not be read.
expectation.conceptual: The package manager should work with packages published using metadata version 2.3. Users should be able to resolve or install dependencies that use that metadata format without the operation failing because the metadata parser is too old.

constraints.grounded: The compatibility change is scoped to requiring a pkginfo version that supports metadata version 2.3 and must not regress handling of packages whose metadata format was already supported before this update. Existing package inspection behavior should remain unchanged except for removing the failure on 2.3 metadata.
constraints.conceptual: This update should expand compatibility for newer package metadata without changing the behavior for packages that were already supported or requiring users to restructure their dependency setup.

behavior: Packages whose distribution metadata version is 2.3 are treated as supported inputs during package information extraction.
Dependency resolution and installation no longer fail solely because a package uses metadata version 2.3.
The runtime dependency floor for pkginfo is raised so environments do not resolve an older metadata parser that lacks version 2.3 support.
acceptance_criteria: When dependency processing encounters a package whose distribution metadata declares version 2.3, it should continue package inspection successfully instead of failing because the package information cannot be created.

When users resolve or install dependencies that include packages with metadata version 2.3, the operation should proceed using the package metadata rather than rejecting that package format as unsupported.
When the application is installed or upgraded, its dependency requirements should prevent use of a pkginfo version older than the first release that supports metadata version 2.3.

task_7.title: Prevent sporadic poetry install crashes from progress output races
task_7.description: Poetry 1.8.3 fixes a race condition during install progress rendering where concurrent output updates could make fancy-output support appear to change during a run, leading to sporadic KeyError failures and aborted installs. The upgrade makes progress-output capability stable for each executor while preserving dry-run and plain-output behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry install` does not sporadically fail with a `KeyError` when concurrent install operations update progress output, and that progress rendering capability is interpreted consistently for the duration of an install run.

expectation.grounded: During `poetry install`, `Executor.supports_fancy_output()` must remain consistent for the lifetime of an executor, based on whether the associated output was decorated when the executor was created and whether the run is not a dry run. Concurrent section-output updates must not change that answer mid-run or leave later progress writes without the expected operation state. Install execution should therefore no longer terminate with a race-induced `KeyError` tied to fancy output handling.
expectation.conceptual: Install runs should treat rich progress output support as a stable capability of the run, not something that can temporarily change while work is already in progress. Temporary terminal-formatting changes during output updates must not crash installation, and dry runs should continue to avoid rich progress behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the dry-run contract of `Executor.supports_fancy_output()`: it must still evaluate to false for dry runs. Executors created with undecorated output must continue to behave without fancy section-based progress handling, and executors created with decorated output must not downgrade or upgrade fancy-output support because of concurrent formatter mutations during progress updates.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must remove instability in progress-output detection without changing whether dry runs use rich output, without requiring decorated terminal support, and without altering normal behavior for environments that already use plain output only.

behavior: `poetry install` no longer crashes with a `KeyError` when concurrent progress-output updates overlap with other install operations.
`Executor.supports_fancy_output()` uses a stable run-level view of output decoration instead of reflecting transient formatter state changes during section updates.
Dry-run execution continues to disable fancy progress output even when the underlying output supports decoration.
Executors created against undecorated output continue to run without assuming decorated section state exists for later progress writes.
acceptance_criteria: Given decorated terminal output and concurrent install progress updates, when `poetry install` runs, then it should complete without a sporadic `KeyError` caused by progress output state changing mid-run.

Given an executor created while decorated output is available, when formatter state is temporarily altered during section updates, then the executor should continue to treat fancy-output support consistently for the remainder of that run.
Given an executor created with undecorated output, when install operations report progress, then the run should behave as a plain-output run and should not assume decorated section state exists.
When install execution is a dry run, it should not enable fancy progress behavior even if decorated output is otherwise available.

task_6.title: Remove false installability warnings from poetry self commands
task_6.description: Poetry 1.8.3 fixes self-management commands so they no longer warn that the current project cannot be installed when Poetry is operating on its own managed environment. The self command workflow now treats that internal project as non-package metadata, preventing a misleading warning while preserving normal self-command execution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that poetry self commands do not emit a misleading warning that the current project cannot be installed when operating on Poetry's own managed environment.

expectation.grounded: Commands in the poetry self workflow that use SelfCommand must treat Poetry's generated tool.poetry project metadata as package-mode = false for the self-managed project. As a result, poetry self operations should no longer report that the current project cannot be installed simply because that internal project is not meant to be installed as a package.
expectation.conceptual: When users run Poetry's self-management commands, Poetry should recognize that its own maintenance project is configuration-only rather than an installable package, and it should stop showing the erroneous installability warning.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to the poetry self command context and must not alter ordinary package-mode behavior for normal user projects. Self-command dependency management and command completion should continue to work, with the warning removed only when it is caused by treating the self-managed project as an installable package.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only correct the self-maintenance workflow and should not change how regular Poetry projects are classified or handled outside that workflow.

behavior: Poetry's self-managed project metadata is handled in non-package mode during poetry self command execution.
poetry self commands no longer emit the warning that the current project cannot be installed when that warning was caused by Poetry evaluating its own internal self project as a package.
Self-command operations continue through their normal dependency-management flow without requiring the self-managed project to be installable as a package.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs a poetry self command, it should not warn that the current project cannot be installed solely because Poetry's self-managed project has no installable package.
When poetry self prepares or uses its internal project metadata, it should treat that metadata as non-package configuration rather than as a package that must be installed.
When users run regular non-self Poetry workflows, their existing package-mode behavior should remain unchanged by this fix.

task_8.title: Correct `poetry shell` help for shell detection and fallback
task_8.description: Poetry 1.8.3 corrects the built-in `poetry shell` guidance so it matches the command's actual behavior. The help text now explains that Poetry starts a shell inside the project's virtual environment, prefers detecting the active shell, falls back to the platform's configured shell environment variable, and still creates a virtual environment when one does not exist.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry shell` provides accurate user-facing guidance about how it chooses and launches a shell inside the project's virtual environment, including the correct platform-specific fallback environment variable and the creation of a virtual environment when one is missing.

expectation.grounded: The public help for `poetry shell` should state that the command spawns a shell within the project's virtual environment, first tries to detect the current active shell, falls back to `SHELL` on non-Windows systems or `COMSPEC` on Windows if detection is unavailable, and indicates that a virtual environment will be created if absent.
expectation.conceptual: Users reading `poetry shell` help should see behavior that matches what the command actually does: Poetry automatically chooses an appropriate shell, only uses the platform shell setting as a fallback, and can create the project environment if needed.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the execution semantics of `poetry shell`, virtual-environment activation handling, or already-activated environment detection as part of this update; only the user-facing command guidance should be corrected to reflect existing behavior.
constraints.conceptual: This update should remove misleading guidance without altering how the command behaves when users actually run it.

behavior: `poetry shell` help describes the command as spawning a shell inside the project's virtual environment.
The documented shell-selection flow says Poetry detects the active shell first and uses the platform shell environment variable only as a fallback.
The fallback environment variable shown in help is platform-specific: `COMSPEC` on Windows and `SHELL` on non-Windows platforms.
The help output indicates that a virtual environment will be created if one does not already exist.
acceptance_criteria: When a user views help for `poetry shell`, it should describe launching a shell within the project's virtual environment.
When a user views help for `poetry shell`, it should describe active-shell detection as the default shell-selection behavior.
When help is viewed on Windows, it should identify `COMSPEC` as the fallback shell environment variable.
When help is viewed on a non-Windows platform, it should identify `SHELL` as the fallback shell environment variable.
When no project virtual environment exists, the help should state that the command will create one.

task_9.title: Document git subdirectory support in poetry add help
task_9.description: Version 1.8.3 improves CLI discoverability by documenting, in the `poetry add` help output, how to reference a dependency located in a subdirectory of a Git repository. This addresses a usability gap where the syntax already existed in broader documentation but was not shown in the command help.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry add` help explains how to add a dependency from a subdirectory within a Git repository so users can discover the supported syntax directly from the CLI.

expectation.grounded: The `poetry add` help output must include Git repository subdirectories as one of the supported dependency forms. The help text should make clear that a Git dependency reference may include a `subdirectory` fragment to target a package below the repository root, alongside the already documented Git URL and revision forms.
expectation.conceptual: Users viewing `poetry add` help should be able to understand, without consulting external documentation, that dependencies can be added from a package living in a subfolder of a Git repository.

constraints.grounded: This update must not alter `poetry add` runtime behavior, dependency resolution semantics, or the availability of other documented package forms; it only extends the command help to cover the existing Git subdirectory syntax.
constraints.conceptual: The change should improve discoverability only. Existing ways of adding dependencies should continue to behave the same, with no new operational requirements introduced by the upgrade.

behavior: `poetry add` help now lists adding a dependency from a Git repository subdirectory as a supported input form.
The help output indicates that Git dependency references may include a subdirectory selector fragment to identify a package that is not stored at the repository root.
The update is limited to user-facing help content and does not introduce new dependency-add behavior beyond documenting an already supported form.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry add --help`, the displayed usage information should explicitly mention adding a dependency from a subdirectory of a Git repository.
When a user reviews the Git-based examples in `poetry add` help, they should be able to infer that a subdirectory can be selected as part of the Git reference.
When upgrading from 1.8.2 to 1.8.3, users should observe improved CLI guidance for Git subdirectory dependencies without any change to normal `poetry add` execution behavior.

task_10.title: Document interactive credential configuration support
task_10.description: Version 1.8.3 adds user-facing documentation clarifying that credential configuration can be performed interactively. The update improves discoverability of an existing capability and does not introduce a runtime behavior change in the provided diff.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users upgrading to 1.8.3 are explicitly informed that credential configuration supports an interactive flow, so authenticated setup is easier to discover and understand.

expectation.grounded: The 1.8.3 release documentation should explicitly mention interactive credential configuration as a supported Poetry workflow. The update should surface the availability of the interactive credential setup experience without implying new runtime APIs, changed command semantics, or modified credential-processing behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to learn from the upgrade guidance that credentials can be configured through an interactive experience, rather than assuming setup is only manual or non-interactive.

constraints.grounded: No runtime behavior change is evidenced in the supplied code diff. The requirement is limited to documenting existing interactive credential configuration support and must not imply new authentication features, altered credential formats, or changed failure behavior.
constraints.conceptual: This update should clarify an existing capability only. It should not suggest that the release changes how credential setup works beyond making the interactive option visible to users.

behavior: The 1.8.3 upgrade materials newly mention that interactive credential configuration is available.
No observable runtime or API behavior changes are indicated by the provided code diff for credential configuration.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reviews the 1.8.3 upgrade or release guidance, it should explicitly communicate that credential configuration can be performed interactively.
When a user compares 1.8.2 to 1.8.3 using the provided artifacts, it should be clear that the change is documentation-focused and does not require application or integration behavior changes.
When users look for credential setup guidance after upgrading, they should be able to discover the interactive configuration option from the release-facing documentation.

task_11.title: Document optional advanced installation steps in 1.8.3
task_11.description: Poetry 1.8.3 adds user-facing documentation for optional advanced installation scenarios. The provided code diff is empty, so this update should be treated as documentation-only with no runtime, API, or behavioral change from 1.8.2.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the 1.8.3 upgrade provides clear guidance for optional advanced installation steps while leaving existing installation and runtime behavior unchanged.

expectation.grounded: The 1.8.3 release should add installation guidance covering optional advanced installation steps. The provided code diff contains no changes, so the upgrade does not evidence any public API, runtime, error-handling, or installer behavior change beyond the added documentation.
expectation.conceptual: Users should find clearer instructions for non-default installation scenarios when reviewing the 1.8.3 guidance, and upgrading should not alter how the library behaves.

constraints.grounded: Do not infer or introduce runtime behavior changes, API additions, changed exceptions, or altered default installation semantics for 1.8.3; the only grounded change is additional documentation for advanced installation options.
constraints.conceptual: Treat this as a documentation-only release item: standard usage should continue to work the same way, with only clearer upgrade and installation guidance added for advanced cases.

behavior: Release documentation includes notes for optional advanced installation steps.
No runtime, public API, or error behavior changes are evidenced between 1.8.2 and 1.8.3 in the provided artifacts.
Default installation and normal library usage remain unchanged; only the available guidance for advanced setup scenarios is expanded.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reviews the 1.8.3 installation guidance, it should include optional advanced installation steps beyond the default setup path.
When upgrading from 1.8.2 to 1.8.3, users should not observe any change in existing runtime or public API behavior.
When users follow the standard installation flow, it should behave the same as before, with additional guidance available only for advanced installation scenarios.

task_12.title: Clarify poetry publish credential setup guidance
task_12.description: Version 1.8.3 updates the Poetry documentation so users of `poetry publish` are directed to the existing credential configuration guidance. The change improves discoverability of authentication setup before publishing and does not introduce a runtime behavior change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the `poetry publish` documentation clearly points users to the credential configuration guidance needed before publishing to authenticated package repositories.

expectation.grounded: The user-facing documentation for `poetry publish` should include a reference to configuring credentials so users can find the relevant authentication setup guidance from the publish workflow documentation. The documented change should not alter the `poetry publish` command surface or its runtime credential-handling behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users preparing to publish packages should be able to discover, from the publish documentation itself, where to set up the credentials required for authenticated publishing. This release should improve guidance only, without changing how publishing behaves.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new `poetry publish` behavior, new credential semantics, or changed command outcomes as part of this upgrade requirement; the scope is limited to documentation that references existing credential configuration guidance.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the upgrade scoped to clearer documentation and preserve existing publishing behavior and authentication rules.

behavior: The `poetry publish` documentation now references credential configuration guidance relevant to publishing with authentication.
The upgrade changes documentation discoverability only and does not add or modify observable runtime behavior in `poetry publish`.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the `poetry publish` documentation, it should direct them to the credential configuration guidance needed for authenticated publishing.
When upgrading from 1.8.2 to 1.8.3, users should observe improved documentation around credential setup for publishing, with no change to the runtime behavior of `poetry publish`.

task_13.title: Clarify environment-variable repository credential setup
task_13.description: Version 1.8.3 is a documentation-focused update. It clarifies how users should configure repository credentials through environment variables, including the relationship between credential configuration and repository URL configuration, without changing runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can understand how to configure repository access credentials through environment variables, including when repository URL configuration also needs to be supplied through environment variables.

expectation.grounded: Document the existing environment-variable-based repository credential configuration more clearly, including the need to account for repository URL configuration when using environment variables. The provided production diff shows no code changes, so the upgrade should not introduce new public APIs or alter credential-handling behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to set up private repository authentication with environment variables from the documentation alone, without ambiguity about whether related repository URL settings also need environment-variable configuration.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the runtime behavior present in 1.8.2 because no production code changes are provided for 1.8.3. Do not add new authentication flows, change credential resolution semantics, or alter repository access behavior as part of this upgrade task.
constraints.conceptual: Treat this release as clarification of existing configuration behavior rather than a functional change. Existing authenticated repository usage should continue to behave the same after upgrading.

behavior: Upgrading from 1.8.2 to 1.8.3 should not change runtime repository authentication behavior.
The user-visible change is improved guidance explaining that repository credentials can be configured through environment variables.
The guidance should also make clear that repository URL configuration may need to be expressed through environment variables alongside credentials.
acceptance_criteria: When users read the 1.8.3 configuration guidance for private repositories, it should explain how to provide credentials through environment variables.
When repository access depends on repository URL configuration, the guidance should make clear that the URL can also be configured through environment variables.
When upgrading an existing setup from 1.8.2 to 1.8.3, repository authentication behavior should remain unchanged at runtime.

task_15.title: Remove outdated keyring backend seeding guidance
task_15.description: Version 1.8.3 removes outdated user guidance around seeding keyring backends. The update clarifies setup expectations for keyring-backed credentials without changing runtime behavior, public APIs, or command semantics.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the 1.8.3 upgrade no longer instructs users to seed project environments with keyring backend packages as part of normal keyring setup, and clarify that this release is a documentation correction rather than a runtime behavior change.

expectation.grounded: User-facing guidance for keyring backends should remove outdated advice about seeding backends into project virtual environments. The release note and empty code diff do not indicate any changes to public APIs, CLI behavior, authentication flow, or keyring integration semantics beyond correcting that guidance.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should clarify how keyring support is described to users and eliminate unnecessary setup advice, while leaving existing library behavior unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new requirements for keyring configuration, new error or warning behavior, or changes to credential resolution. Preserve existing runtime behavior and compatibility because no production code change is evidenced in this update.
constraints.conceptual: Treat this release as a documentation-only clarification. Existing keyring-backed workflows should continue to behave exactly as before.

behavior: User-facing upgrade or setup guidance no longer advises seeding project virtual environments with keyring backend packages.
No observable runtime, API, or command behavior change is introduced by the 1.8.2 to 1.8.3 update.
acceptance_criteria: When users review the 1.8.3 upgrade notes or setup guidance, it should no longer tell them to seed project environments with keyring backend packages.
When users upgrade from 1.8.2 to 1.8.3, existing keyring-backed authentication workflows should continue to behave the same way.
The upgrade should not require users to perform any new runtime configuration step for keyring support beyond following current, accurate guidance.

task_14.title: Clarify Poetry virtual environment guidance
task_14.description: Poetry 1.8.3 updates the FAQ for disabling managed virtual environments so it no longer suggests that containerized workflows generally justify turning them off. The docs now describe disabling automatic environment creation as an exception for rare cases and reaffirm that using a virtual environment remains the recommended practice, even inside containers, whether managed by Poetry or another tool.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry's user guidance for virtual environments no longer implies that containers are a normal reason to disable Poetry-managed virtual environments, and clearly states when disabling them is appropriate.

expectation.grounded: The FAQ entry for disabling Poetry-managed virtual environments should present the `virtualenvs.create` setting as a way to stop Poetry from creating a managed virtual environment only in rare scenarios where a Poetry-managed environment is not possible or not preferred. It should explicitly state that the recommended best practice is still to use a virtual environment, including when installing an application in a container, and that the environment may be managed by Poetry or by another tool.
expectation.conceptual: Users should understand that disabling Poetry's automatic virtual environment creation is an exception, not the default recommendation. Container-based workflows should still be documented as compatible with using a virtual environment.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the documented effect of the `virtualenvs.create` setting: it remains the mechanism for disabling Poetry-managed virtual environment creation. Preserve the distinction between turning off Poetry's management of a virtual environment and not using any virtual environment at all.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing configuration behavior intact while correcting the guidance. The update should clarify recommendation and scope without implying a runtime change.

behavior: The documentation describing disabled virtual environment management should characterize it as intended for uncommon cases where Poetry should not create the environment.
The documentation should no longer cite container usage as a general reason to avoid virtual environments.
The documentation should state that using a virtual environment remains the recommended practice even in containerized installations.
The documentation should make clear that the virtual environment can be provided by Poetry or by a different environment-management tool.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the FAQ about disabling Poetry-managed virtual environments, it should describe the `virtualenvs.create` setting as an exception for rare or constrained scenarios.
When a user looks for guidance on running Poetry in containers, the documentation should recommend using a virtual environment rather than implying that containers justify disabling one.
When a user disables Poetry's virtual environment creation, the documentation should still distinguish that choice from the broader best practice of using an isolated environment.
When a user relies on another environment manager, the documentation should acknowledge that this still satisfies the recommendation to use a virtual environment.

task_16.title: Clarify multiple extras syntax in pyproject.toml
task_16.description: Version 1.8.3 clarifies how to declare a dependency with multiple extras in pyproject.toml so users do not confuse TOML dependency syntax with the CLI --extras syntax and accidentally omit required optional dependencies.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that documentation for dependency extras clearly shows how to declare multiple extras for a single dependency in pyproject.toml, and distinguish that format from the Poetry CLI extras syntax to prevent missing dependencies caused by configuration mistakes.

expectation.grounded: Documentation should include a pyproject.toml example of one dependency declared with more than one extra in its extras field. The guidance should make clear that, in pyproject.toml, extras are expressed as individually quoted values in a comma-separated list, and that this differs from the format used with the Poetry CLI --extras option.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to look at the dependency extras documentation and correctly configure multiple extras on a single dependency without inferring CLI syntax rules for project configuration.

constraints.grounded: This update is documentation-only and should not change dependency resolution behavior, the meaning of extras, or the existing CLI interface for installing extras. The documented example must remain consistent with supported Poetry dependency declaration syntax.
constraints.conceptual: The change should improve clarity only. It must not alter how extras work or introduce any new configuration behavior.

behavior: Documentation presents an example of a single dependency configured with multiple extras in pyproject.toml.
Documentation explicitly distinguishes pyproject.toml extras formatting from Poetry CLI extras formatting.
The documented guidance reduces the risk that users omit optional dependencies because they copied CLI-style extras syntax into project configuration.
No runtime or dependency resolution behavior changes are introduced by this update.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the dependency extras documentation, they can see an example of one dependency declared with multiple extras in pyproject.toml.
When comparing pyproject.toml configuration with Poetry CLI usage, the documentation makes it clear that the two syntaxes are formatted differently.
When a user follows the documented pyproject.toml example, they can represent multiple extras for a dependency without ambiguity.
The 1.8.3 update does not change production behavior beyond clarifying documentation.

task_18.title: Document TestPyPI credential setup for poetry publish
task_18.description: Poetry 1.8.3 adds user-facing guidance for configuring credentials when publishing packages to TestPyPI with `poetry publish`. The update clarifies an existing workflow and does not introduce runtime or API changes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users publishing to TestPyPI with `poetry publish` can understand how to configure authentication credentials without ambiguity.

expectation.grounded: The upgrade should provide user-facing guidance that explains how TestPyPI credentials are configured for `poetry publish`. This guidance should cover the authentication setup needed for the TestPyPI target while preserving the existing `poetry publish` command behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Publishing to TestPyPI should be clearly documented so users know how to supply credentials and can use `poetry publish` against that repository without guesswork.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new runtime behavior, command options, or authentication flows for `poetry publish`; the change is limited to clarifying existing TestPyPI credential configuration. Existing publish behavior for other repositories must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: This update should improve clarity only. It must not change how publishing works or alter established publishing workflows.

behavior: Adds explicit user-facing guidance for configuring authentication credentials when `poetry publish` targets TestPyPI.
Leaves the observable runtime behavior and public interface of `poetry publish` unchanged.
Reduces ambiguity around publishing to TestPyPI by documenting the required credential setup rather than introducing new publishing mechanics.
acceptance_criteria: When a user wants to publish to TestPyPI with `poetry publish`, the available upgrade documentation should explain how credentials are configured for that repository.
When users follow the documented TestPyPI credential setup, they should not need to infer a separate or undocumented authentication mechanism for `poetry publish`.
Upgrading from 1.8.2 to 1.8.3 should not change the runtime behavior or public command surface of `poetry publish`; the observable change should be documentation clarity.

task_17.title: Clarify `poetry add` help to mention installation
task_17.description: Version 1.8.3 updates the user-facing CLI description for `poetry add` so help output and command listings clearly state that the command both records the dependency in `pyproject.toml` and installs it in the relevant environment. This aligns the help text with the command's existing behavior and reduces ambiguity for users.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the `poetry add` command help clearly communicates that adding a dependency also installs it, so the CLI description matches the command's actual behavior.

expectation.grounded: The public description shown for `poetry add`, including in `poetry add --help` and command listings such as `poetry list`, should state that the command adds a dependency to `pyproject.toml` and installs it. The command's functional behavior does not otherwise change.
expectation.conceptual: Users should see unambiguous CLI guidance that `poetry add` both registers a dependency in the project configuration and installs it, with consistent wording wherever the command is summarized.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new `poetry add` options, arguments, or execution semantics. Dependency addition, environment installation behavior, and other command behavior must remain unchanged aside from the clarified user-facing description.
constraints.conceptual: This update should improve the accuracy of the command help without changing the workflow or adding new behavior.

behavior: The user-visible summary for `poetry add` now communicates two outcomes: updating `pyproject.toml` and installing the dependency.
The clarified description is reflected in the CLI surfaces that expose the command summary, including `poetry add --help` and command listings.
No new dependency-management behavior is introduced; the change is limited to making existing behavior explicit in the help text.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry add --help`, the command description should indicate that the command both adds the dependency to `pyproject.toml` and installs it.
When a user views the CLI command list, the `add` entry should present the same combined description of adding and installing.
When a user runs `poetry add`, the command should continue to behave as before, with this upgrade only clarifying the help text rather than changing dependency resolution or installation behavior.

task_19.title: Clarify README extension support in poetry new
task_19.description: Poetry 1.8.3 corrects the user-facing contract for `poetry new --readme`. The option should be understood as choosing the README file extension with `md` as the default, not as a setting limited to only Markdown or reStructuredText.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry new --readme` is presented and supported as a general README file extension option with `md` as the default, instead of implying that only `md` and `rst` are valid values.

expectation.grounded: The public behavior of `poetry new` should treat `--readme` as an option for specifying the README file format or extension, with `md` as the default when the option is omitted. User-facing help for `--readme` should no longer state or imply that the accepted values are limited to `md` and `rst`, and non-default extensions should remain supported inputs for README generation.
expectation.conceptual: Users creating a new project should be able to choose the README extension they want. The command should communicate that Markdown is the default, while not misleading users into thinking the option only supports two predefined formats.

constraints.grounded: Keep the default `poetry new` README behavior as `md` when `--readme` is not provided. Do not narrow `--readme` to an enumerated set of extensions in public help or behavior, and do not change unrelated `poetry new` command semantics.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve the existing default behavior while removing misleading restrictions from the user-facing contract. The update should clarify supported input without changing unrelated project creation behavior.

behavior: `poetry new --help` should describe `--readme` as defaulting to `md` instead of presenting only `md` and `rst` as valid formats.
The documented contract for `--readme` should allow arbitrary README extensions rather than a fixed two-value set.
Omitting `--readme` should continue to produce the default Markdown README behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user views help for `poetry new`, the `--readme` option should indicate that `md` is the default and should not claim that only `md` or `rst` are supported.
When a user runs `poetry new` without `--readme`, it should continue to use a Markdown README by default.
When a user supplies `poetry new --readme` with a non-default extension, the option should be treated as a supported README extension choice rather than being described as outside the supported set.

task_21.title: Clarify pipx-based Poetry plugin uninstall flow
task_21.description: Version 1.8.3 updates the user guidance for removing Poetry plugins when Poetry is managed with pipx. The release aligns the documented uninstall flow with pipx 1.2.0+, which removes injected packages through `pipx uninject`, and does not introduce a runtime behavior change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users managing Poetry plugins through pipx are given the correct uninstall flow for injected plugins, so plugin removal guidance matches the pipx command intended for removing previously injected packages.

expectation.grounded: For Poetry installations managed via `pipx`, the documented plugin removal flow should identify `pipx uninject` as the supported way to remove a previously injected plugin package when using `pipx` 1.2.0 or newer.
expectation.conceptual: Users who add Poetry plugins through pipx should be told the correct way to remove them, using pipx's injected-package removal workflow rather than outdated uninstall guidance.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce or imply changes to Poetry's plugin APIs, loading behavior, or runtime uninstall semantics; the update is limited to the documented pipx command used for removing injected plugin packages.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the change non-breaking and documentation-focused: only correct the user-facing uninstall instructions for pipx-managed plugins, without changing how plugins work.

behavior: Poetry plugin uninstall guidance for `pipx`-managed environments now points users to `pipx uninject` for removing injected plugin packages.
The documented removal flow explicitly reflects the `pipx` capability added in version 1.2.0 for uninstalling previously injected packages.
No runtime change to Poetry plugin installation, discovery, loading, or execution is introduced by this update.
acceptance_criteria: When a user follows 1.8.3 guidance to remove a Poetry plugin from a `pipx`-managed Poetry installation, the documented command should be `pipx uninject`.
When the plugin was previously added as an injected package, the removal guidance should describe pipx's injected-package removal flow rather than an outdated or generic uninstall path.
Upgrading from 1.8.2 to 1.8.3 should not change observable plugin runtime behavior; the only user-visible change is corrected uninstall guidance.

task_20.title: Clarify Poetry Python Constraint Semantics
task_20.description: Poetry 1.8.3 clarifies that the project's `python` dependency entry expresses which interpreter versions the project supports. It does not make Poetry install or manage Python itself, so users still need a compatible interpreter available when installing or working with the project environment.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry clearly communicates that the project's Python constraint is a compatibility declaration rather than a managed dependency, so users understand they must provide a compatible interpreter themselves.

expectation.grounded: User-facing guidance should state that the `python` constraint in `tool.poetry.dependencies` defines the supported Python interpreter range for the project. When `poetry install` runs, Poetry should rely on an already available interpreter that satisfies that constraint and should not be represented as downloading, installing, or downgrading Python on the user's behalf. Guidance may point users who manage interpreters externally to the `virtualenvs.prefer-active-python` workflow.
expectation.conceptual: Users should understand that setting a Python version in Poetry describes which interpreter versions the project supports. Installing the project depends on having a matching Python already present, not on Poetry treating Python like a normal package dependency that it will fetch or switch automatically.

constraints.grounded: Do not change dependency or interpreter-management behavior in this update. The declared Python range should continue to act as a project compatibility constraint, and Poetry should continue to require a matching local interpreter rather than adding automatic Python provisioning.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only remove ambiguity about Python version handling. It should not introduce new environment management behavior or change how users obtain Python itself.

behavior: The project's `python` dependency entry represents the range of supported Python interpreter versions rather than an installable package.
Running `poetry install` requires access to an installed Python interpreter that satisfies the declared project constraint.
Poetry does not automatically install, replace, or downgrade Python interpreters to satisfy the declared constraint.
Users who manage Python versions with external tooling may prefer an already active interpreter instead of expecting Poetry to provision Python.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project that declares a supported Python range, when a compatible interpreter is already installed locally, `poetry install` should treat that declaration as a compatibility constraint and proceed without implying that Poetry installed Python itself.

Given a project whose declared Python range is not satisfied by any available local interpreter, when `poetry install` is run, Poetry should still require the user to supply a matching interpreter instead of provisioning one automatically.

When users change the declared Python version for a project, Poetry should continue to interpret that setting as the supported interpreter range for the project rather than as a request to manage Python like a normal dependency.
When users manage interpreters with an external tool, Poetry should remain compatible with workflows that prefer the currently active interpreter.
